page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for high-density computational workloads. It features 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8570 processors running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 480.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs, delivering a combined 384 GB of VRAM.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring 97240.84 in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and 88533.65 in Passmark CPU testing. Memory performance is notable, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching a top-tier 385.14 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads reach 7105.96 GB/sec. Large-scale data processing is supported by a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 706.88 GB/sec and database operations scoring 33288.64 on Passmark. For AI workloads, prompt processing for a small 135M LLM model achieves 9458.91 tokens/sec.

From a resource-density perspective, the server offers high-tier GPU and memory capacity, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for massive parallel processing tasks. However, architectural tradeoffs include a shared CPU allocation model and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data.

This configuration is suited for large-scale artificial intelligence workloads, including LLM inference, deep learning training, and high-performance computing simulations. It is also highly capable of handling memory-intensive database operations, complex cryptographic tasks, and parallel data decompression pipelines.
description: The UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-480GB-2xB200 is a high-performance GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 physical Intel Xeon 8570 cores operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 480.0 GB of system memory. The primary computational accelerators are two NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs providing 384 GB of total VRAM. In benchmarks, the server excels in multi-threaded tasks, achieving top-tier results in Passmark CPU scores, large-block memory read bandwidth at 385.14 GB/sec, and LLM prompt processing at 9458.91 tokens/sec. Tradeoffs include a shared CPU allocation and the absence of local storage. This server is optimized for deep learning, large-scale LLM inference, parallel data processing, and memory-intensive database operations.
